entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner was the original 7th accused in C.C No.2352/2016 on the file of the Court of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kuthuparamba ('Trial Court' in short), which was filed by the 2nd respondent alleging the commission of the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, and 120 (B) of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Court of the Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kuthuparamba
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As the petitioner was alleged to be absconding, the case against her was split up and the trial proceeded against the other accused, who have been acquitted by Annexure B judgment.

The case against the petitioner has now been renumbered as C.C. No.
1404/2025.
2.
The prosecution case, in Annexure A complaint is that, the accused nos. 1 to 5 were conducting a financial institution named as Kalpetta 2026:KER:11018 Janakshema Maruthi Chits Pvt. Ltd.

entities.text: Kalpetta 2026:KER:11018 Janakshema Maruthi Chits Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: The 1st accused is the company, the 2nd accused its Managing Director, accused nos. 3 to 5 are Directors, the 6th accused is a Legal Manager and the 7th accused is an office staff.
The accused persons collected money from the public by conducting Chitti business.
The accused no. 6 and 7 had approached the complainant and induced him to join the Chitti, on a false assurance that he would be given good returns.
Accordingly, the 2nd respondent deposited the money with the 1st accused company.
However, the accused persons allegedly failed to pay the money and refused to return the capital.
Thus, the accused have committed the above offences.
3. The petitioner has stated in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case that she was only an employee of the 1st accused company.
Although, she had got herself enlarged on bail at the crime stage, subsequently she did not receive any summons from the Trial Court.
Consequently, the case against her was split up and the 2026:KER:11018 trial against the other accused progressed and was concluded by the Trial Court.

4. By Annexure B judgment, the Trial Court, on finding that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt against the 6th accused and acquitted him of the above offences.
By Annexure B judgment, the substratum of the prosecution case has been lost.

Therefore,
even if the petitioner withstands the ordeal of trial, it is not going to yield a different result than Annexure B judgment.
Hence, the entire proceedings as against the petitioner may be quashed.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned public prosecutor.

6. The complaint was taken on file by the Trial Court on the basis of Annexure A, a private complaint filed by the 2nd respondent, alleging that the petitioner and the other accused persons had committed the above 2026:KER:11018 mentioned offences.

sentences.text:
In Moosa V. Sub Inspector of Police (2006 (1) KLT 552), a full Bench of this Court has held that,
in a case where the very substratum of the case is lost by the acquittal of the co-accused, the inherent power of this Court can be exercised to quash the proceedings against the other accused persons.

entities.text: Moosa V. Sub Inspector of Police (2006 (1) KLT 552)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same view has been reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and this Court in a plethora of precedents on the above question of law.

8. By Annexure B judgment, the Trial Court, after analysing the materials on record, came to the conclusion that, although Pws 1 to 3 were examined, no material was produced by them to prove that the accused persons had hatched a conspiracy or had cheated the 2nd respondent.
Consequently, the 6 th accused was acquitted.
9. I have carefully gone through the allegations in Annexure A complaint and the findings in Annexure B 2026:KER:11018 judgment.
10. A reading of Annexure B judgment clearly establishes that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove that the accused persons had committed the offences alleged against them.
11. In light of the findings in Annexure B judgment, I am satisfied that the substratum of the prosecution case has been lost.
Therefore, the findings in the said judgment is clearly applicable to the petitioner also.
Even if the petitioner withstands the ordeal of trial, it will not yield a different result than Annexure B judgment.
Thus, I am convinced and satisfied that the findings in Annexure B judgment would enure to the benefit of the petitioner also.
It would only be a sheer waste of judicial time to conduct the trial all over again for the petitioner.

Thus, I am inclined to allow the Crl.M.C by exercising the inherent powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS.
2026

In the above circumstances, the Crl.M.C is allowed and consequently, Annexure A complaint and all further proceedings in C.C. No. 1404/2025 on the file of the Trial Court, as against the petitioner, are quashed.
